title: A persistently failing store save is logged only at DEBUG at all 17 persist handlers; state stops persisting
claim: Every persist handler (17, persist_seams.py) catches any exception from building and saving its store payload and logs it only at DEBUG; with the save body forced to fail on every pass across setup, two refreshes, unload, restart and a refresh, each of the 10 handlers the lifecycle reaches added zero WARNING-or-higher records, so a payload-builder bug or a failing save silently stops the ledger, accuracy, thermal-learning, price-model, snapshot, away, legionella, notifier, off-restore and energy stores from persisting until a restart loses the unsaved state.
mechanism: Pattern `try: await store.async_save(<payload built inline>) except Exception as err: _LOGGER.debug('Could not persist ...: %s', err)` in coordinator._async_save_{thermal_learning,price_model,ledger,accuracy,energy_totals,manual_plan,snapshots}, away.persist_override, boost.persist, dhw_learning.async_save_{profile,draws}, duty_switch._persist, legionella.async_save, notifier._async_save, off_restore._save, pump_arbiter._persist, debugger.DebugCollector.async_save. The payload is built inside the try, so a programming error in any learner's as_dict (an AttributeError, a non-serialisable value) is caught with the transport failures and logged below Home Assistant's default level on every cycle; nothing latches it (log_held exists for exactly this) and no repair issue is raised.

evidence.unit: persist handlers (of 10 reached) whose persistent save failure added no WARNING+ record
evidence.machine: orchestrator Mac, Apple M1 (darwin arm64, 8 cores), shared box

instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._async_save_ledger (and the 9 sibling persist handlers), each try body forced to raise by d1s3hook.py's import-time rewrite, driven through async_setup_entry / async_refresh / async_unload_entry on a real asyncio loop

perturbation.change: coordinator.py: `_LOGGER.debug("Could not persist ledger: %s", err)` -> `_LOGGER.warning(...)` (`--perturb`, applied in memory at import via excepts_inject.py --edit)

metric_definition: Persist handlers reached by the lifecycle whose save body, raising on every pass (setup, 2 refreshes, unload, restart, refresh), added 0 WARNING+ integration records over the control.
phenomenon_property: A persistent store-save failure is visible above DEBUG once per outage (a held warning that says Resolved on the first save that lands), at every persist seam.

null_control.note: the fault-free control run is the baseline every added-record count is taken over; the same harness counts WARNING+ for the weather fetch handler (coordinator.py:7103) at 1 per outage, so the count is able to see a warning

proposed_fix_scope: One held-warning helper (log_latch.log_held) across the 17 persist handlers, keyed per store; optionally build the payload outside the try so a builder bug is not filed as a save failure.
